title: QUIC RFC 9000 Zero-Length Connection-ID Mode Runtime Work Item
summary: Implement and prove bounded zero-length connection-ID mode behavior for local CID issuance suppression and outbound empty Destination Connection ID selection toward peers that selected zero-length mode.
planned_changes:
- Add a runtime helper that identifies local zero-length connection-ID selection from committed local transport parameters.
- Reject explicit local connection-ID issuance after local zero-length selection.
- Reject automatic local connection-ID replenishment after local zero-length selection.
- Install an empty handshake destination connection ID when committed peer transport parameters select zero-length mode.
- Make CurrentPeerDestinationConnectionId prefer empty output for peer zero-length mode before peer-issued CID, preferred-address, or handshake fallback state.
- Add positive, negative, and edge requirement-home tests for REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S5P1P1-0020 and REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S5P1P1-0021.
verification_plan: Run the focused zero-length connection-ID requirement homes and nearby connection-ID/migration regression homes, build the solution, validate canonical SpecTrace JSON, and run `git diff --check`.
out_of_scope: Public API selection of local zero-length mode.
Broad active migration support for zero-length connection-ID deployments.
completion_notes: Completed as a bounded runtime slice. Local zero-length mode now suppresses explicit and replenishment issuance, and peer zero-length mode installs an empty outbound Destination Connection ID through the runtime peer transport-parameter commit path.
